verdict.summary: Creating an app and connecting your own account is quick. Public distribution is the hard part: unlisted apps are capped at 25 installs, and a Marketplace listing needs a manual Ecosystem Quality review, at least three real active unaffiliated installs, OAuth as the only auth method, and no sensitive-data scopes.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1 day for app setup and listing prep, plus time to gather real installs (not counted above)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 minutes once the developer account exists
verdict.approval_wait: None for own-account or private (allowlisted) use. Marketplace listing: HubSpot's initial review target is 10 business days, and resubmission may extend it. Certification is optional and adds at least six months.

gates.name: Own account (development)
gates.unlocks: Create the app and install it into your own HubSpot account, then connect it through Composio. Developer test accounts do not count toward install caps.
limits: Apps created or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace.
Standard-account installs must be done by a Super Admin or a user with the HubSpot Marketplace access permission.
Access and refresh token lifetimes were not confirmed.

gates.name: Private distribution (allowlisted accounts)
gates.unlocks: Install the app in up to 10 allowlisted customer accounts with a privately distributed OAuth app. Apps created in a Solutions Partner portal can reach up to 100 customer portals.
limits: Up to 10 allowlisted accounts for privately distributed OAuth.
The Solutions Partner 100-portal limit does not apply to static-token private apps.
Sensitive scopes need access requested from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team (see scopes).
A private project app can later be switched to Marketplace distribution without interrupting installs (community source).
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as setup; no HubSpot review step was found for private distribution

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public installs)
gates.unlocks: Unlimited installs by any HubSpot account once the listing is approved. Users see a confirmation dialog for apps not reviewed by the Marketplace quality team.
limits: Listing is manually reviewed by the Ecosystem Quality team and rejected if criteria are not met.
Only one app can be submitted at a time; extra submissions are automatically rejected.
Installs must be unique production accounts unaffiliated with you, with successful activity in the past 30 days.
Per installing account rate limit: 110 requests every 10 seconds, excluding the CRM Search API.
Certification (optional, higher tier) requires six months listed and at least 60 active unique installs, plus a demo video, security questionnaire and verified domain.
gates.time_to_reach: About 10 business days for the initial review, after at least three active unaffiliated installs are in place

steps.title: Create or confirm your HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign in to (or create) a HubSpot developer account. You need it to create and manage apps in the developer portal. Confirm the portal ID you will build in, since the Applications page URL includes it.
gotchas: Exact requirements (free account, paid plan, or Super Admin role) were not confirmed from an official page. Check with HubSpot if your account lacks access.

steps.title: Create the app and choose distribution
steps.detail: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI or the Applications page in the developer portal. When asked, choose whether to distribute on the Marketplace or restrict installation to specific accounts. A private app can be switched to Marketplace later.
gotchas: Apps created or migrated to 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed, so choosing Marketplace at setup does not lift the cap by itself.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: Add the redirect URL in the app's auth config (redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json, or the Redirect URL field on the Auth tab in the older flow). It must use HTTPS; http://localhost is allowed for testing only. Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Each app needs at least one redirect URL, and it must use HTTPS.

steps.title: Declare only the scopes the app uses
steps.detail: Open the app in the Development section, then the Auth tab. Review the Scopes section and select only required, conditionally required and optional scopes your app actually uses. Do not copy Composio's default scope list.

values.label: Required scopes
values.value: At least one required scope must be declared. Limit the rest to what your agent calls.

gotchas: Apps must use every scope they request during installation. Remove unused scopes before listing.
Composio's default set includes settings.users.write and many CRM write scopes.

steps.title: Install into your own account and capture the token exchange
steps.detail: Copy the install URL from the app's settings and open it while signed in to your own HubSpot account. The authorize redirect returns a code, which is exchanged for access and refresh tokens. Confirm the connection works end to end before you go further.

values.label: Token URL (from Composio config, not checked on a HubSpot page)

gotchas: Installer must be a Super Admin or have the Marketplace access permission.
Token lifetimes were not confirmed; test refresh before relying on it.

steps.title: Connect the app through Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom auth config for the hubspot toolkit using your app's client ID and client secret. Use Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app instead if you only need to prototype against accounts you control.
gotchas: The Composio custom-auth UI steps were not part of this research. Verify field names in Composio's docs.

steps.title: Draft listing and privacy materials
steps.detail: An agent can draft the privacy policy, terms of service, listing description, and a scope justification for each scope the app keeps. Host the terms and privacy policy on live URLs before submission. Each URL field is limited to 250 characters.
gotchas: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs must be live and up to date.
Logos must be your own and must not combine HubSpot's name with your app name.

steps.title: Invite up to 10 allowlisted accounts for testing
steps.detail: Add the accounts you want to test with, up to 10 for a privately distributed OAuth app. Solutions Partners can use a partner portal to reach up to 100 customer portals. Confirm each install works and log the OAuth calls, since they count toward activity.
gotchas: Developer test accounts do not count toward the caps, but customer accounts do.
Sensitive scopes need Ecosystem Quality allowlisting before testing with them.

steps.title: Get at least three real, active, unaffiliated installs
steps.detail: Listing requires at least three unique production installs that are not affiliated with your organization and show successful app activity in the past 30 days. Activity includes OAuth API calls and signed webhook or card requests. Plan for this before you submit.
gotchas: This is the chicken-and-egg point: you cannot list without installs, and the 25-install cap applies until the listing is approved.

steps.title: Remove sensitive-data scopes
steps.detail: Confirm the app does not request, use or access sensitive data scopes. Remove any such scopes from the Auth tab. Agent tool listings also must not use them.
gotchas: Research found conflicting guidance on whether 2025.2 apps can get sensitive scopes approved for Marketplace listing. Do not rely on approval.
Sensitive data also requires an Enterprise subscription on the installing account.

steps.title: Record a demo video or guided walkthrough
steps.detail: Record a short demo of the app's core flows, or write a guided walkthrough document, and attach it to the listing submission. Certification will not be reviewed without a demo video.
gotchas: The demo-video requirement for listing comes from a third-party source (March 2026). Verify it in the listing form.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Submit the listing in the developer portal. Confirm you have agreed to HubSpot's Technology Partner Program Agreement. Only one app can be in review at a time, so do not submit a second app until the first is decided.
gotchas: Classic CRM cards are not supported since June 16, 2025.
Extra submissions while one is processing are automatically rejected.

steps.title: Wait for the initial Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team manually reviews the listing, with an initial review target of 10 business days from submission. HubSpot will contact you if information is incorrect, misleading or incomplete.

steps.title: Optional: apply for certification
steps.detail: Certification is above the basic listing and is not needed for public installs. It reviews security, privacy, reliability, performance, usability, accessibility and value. It needs a verified domain, a security best-practices assessment, and a security questionnaire covering encryption, access controls and token lifecycle. Certifications are valid for two years.
gotchas: Requires six months listed and at least 60 active unique unaffiliated installs.
HubSpot may reject certification requests at its discretion; only one app can be submitted for certification at a time.

requirements.detail: Needed to create and manage apps. Exact account type and role requirements were not confirmed.

Every app needs at least one redirect URL using HTTPS; http://localhost is allowed for testing.

requirements.item: Install cap for unlisted OAuth apps
requirements.detail: 25 accounts before Marketplace listing; 10 allowlisted accounts for private OAuth distribution.

Must review and agree to the terms, and avoid restricted industries.
Marketplace listing requires the app to not access, request or use sensitive data scopes.

Required for certification. Reported as part of the listing submission, from a third-party source.

requirements.detail: Certification-tier requirements, not required for a basic listing.

requirements.detail: Applies only if sensitive-data scopes are used.

scopes.effect: Standard CRM object scopes. Tier not classified in research. Request only if your agent reads or writes these objects; unused scopes must be removed before listing.
In Composio's default set. Do not request it unless the app manages users; it is a write scope that reviewers will question without a clear use case.
Broad by design for a managed app. A custom app should narrow scopes to its actual use.
Not allowed on a Marketplace listing. Requires Ecosystem Quality allowlisting for testing, and the installing account needs an Enterprise subscription. Naming example is from a third-party blog.

scopes.scope: Any scope on an agent tool listing
scopes.effect: Agent tool listings must not access, request or use sensitive data scopes at this time.

blockers.symptom: Install fails or is blocked after 25 accounts on a 2025.2 app.
blockers.cause: Apps created or migrated to 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Plan for the cap. Get a Marketplace listing approved to remove it, or use private distribution (10 allowlisted accounts) for smaller rollouts.

blockers.symptom: Cannot submit for listing: not enough installs.
blockers.cause: Listing requires at least three unique, unaffiliated, active installs with activity in the past 30 days.
blockers.fix: Get three real customer accounts installed and making successful OAuth calls within 30 days before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected by Ecosystem Quality review.
blockers.cause: Submission did not meet the listing criteria, e.g. sensitive scopes requested, unused scopes, non-OAuth auth, or live policy URLs missing.
blockers.fix: Remove sensitive-data scopes and unused scopes, make sure both policy URLs are live, and resubmit. Watch for HubSpot's contact if information is incomplete.

blockers.symptom: Second app submission is automatically rejected.
blockers.cause: Only one app can be submitted at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the first submission to be decided before submitting another.

blockers.symptom: Users see a confirmation dialog before installing your app.
blockers.cause: Since March 23, 2026, HubSpot shows this dialog for third-party apps not reviewed by the Marketplace quality team.
blockers.fix: Expect this until the listing is approved. Explain it in your onboarding copy.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app to prototype or to connect accounts you control. Build your own HubSpot app when you need to install beyond the caps (25 unlisted, 10 allowlisted), list on the Marketplace, or use a Solutions Partner portal. Composio's default scope list is broad, so a custom app should request only the scopes it uses.

evidence.claim: Apps created or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace; the cap started Sept 22, 2025.
evidence.quote: apps that are created or migrated to version 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Initial listing review target is 10 business days from submission; HubSpot contacts the developer if information is incorrect, misleading or incomplete.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

evidence.claim: Minimum listing requirements: OAuth as the sole authorization method; one public app ID / OAuth client ID per listing; unique use case with no duplicate apps; only scopes the app needs; at least three active unique installs.
evidence.quote: your app must use OAuth as its sole authorization method.

evidence.claim: Active installs must be unique production accounts unaffiliated with the developer's organization with successful app activity in the past 30 days; activity includes OAuth API calls and signed webhook or card requests.
evidence.quote: Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, showing successful app activity within the past 30 days.

evidence.claim: Listing also requires agreeing to HubSpot's Technology Partner Program Agreement, avoiding restricted industries, and not using classic CRM cards (unsupported since June 16, 2025).
evidence.quote: you must review and agree to the terms in HubSpot’s Technology Partner Program Agreement.

evidence.claim: Listing content must be complete and accurate; Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs must be live and up to date; URL fields are limited to 250 characters; logos must be your own and must not combine HubSpot's name with your app name.
evidence.quote: URLs for your app’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.

evidence.claim: Certification (above basic listing) reviews security, privacy, reliability, performance, usability, accessibility and value. It requires OAuth with all required scopes, a verified domain, and passing a security best-practices assessment (outdated software and web server vulnerabilities).
evidence.quote: Pass an assessment for security best practices related to outdated software and various web server vulnerabilities and findings.

evidence.claim: Certification also requires a security questionnaire covering encryption, access controls and OAuth token lifecycle management.
evidence.quote: You must also complete a security questionnaire addressing questions of encryption, access controls, and token lifecycle management

evidence.claim: Certification requires the app to have been listed on the Marketplace for at least six months and to have at least 60 active, unique, unaffiliated installs to qualify and retain certification.
evidence.quote: Your app must have at least 60 active, unique installs to qualify for and retain certification.

evidence.claim: HubSpot will not review a certification request without a demo video; it may reject certification requests at its discretion; only one app may be submitted for certification at a time; certifications are valid for two years and must be renewed.
evidence.quote: HubSpot will not review your app unless you submit a demo video as instructed

evidence.claim: Certified apps must be associated with a verified domain, and the verification steps are documented in the app-management docs.
evidence.quote: Be associated with a verified domain.

evidence.claim: Install caps by type: Marketplace OAuth app before listing = 25 accounts; after listing = unlimited; privately distributed OAuth = up to 10 allowlisted accounts; static token app = 1 standard account plus up to 10 developer test accounts (test accounts not counted in the caps).
evidence.quote: Marketplace OAuth app prior to listing: can be installed in up to 25 accounts (not including developer test accounts).

evidence.claim: Third-party guidance: the listing submission includes a demo video or guided walkthrough; test credentials reportedly no longer required from March 2026 (not confirmed on an official page).
evidence.quote: You now provide a demo video showing your app's core flows or a guided walkthrough doc.

evidence.claim: Since March 23, 2026, HubSpot shows users a confirmation dialog before installing third-party apps not reviewed by the Marketplace Ecosystem Quality team.
evidence.quote: We’ve added a confirmation dialog when HubSpot users install third-party apps that haven’t been reviewed by HubSpot’s Marketplace quality team.

evidence.claim: Marketplace-distributed OAuth apps on platform 2025.2 and 2026.03 are rate-limited per installing account to 110 requests every 10 seconds, excluding the CRM Search API.
evidence.quote: each HubSpot account that installs your app is limited to 110 requests every 10 seconds.

evidence.claim: Sensitive-data scopes: an app must not access, request or use sensitive data scopes to be listed on the Marketplace.
evidence.quote: Your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: Legacy and 2025.2 / 2026.03 apps intended for Marketplace must request specific sensitive scopes from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, who allowlist them for testing and approve publication after compliance checks; sensitive data access also needs an Enterprise subscription on the installing account.
evidence.quote: you’ll need to request access to specific sensitive scopes from HubSpot’s Ecosystem Quality team.

evidence.claim: The installing HubSpot account must have an Enterprise subscription to access Sensitive Data functionality.
evidence.quote: The HubSpot account must have an Enterprise subscription to access Sensitive Data functionality.

evidence.claim: Sensitive-data scopes are named by object and access level, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read (third-party blog).
evidence.quote: crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read

evidence.claim: Agent tool listings must not access, request or use sensitive data scopes at this time.
evidence.quote: at this time, your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: Listing and security rules require apps to use all scopes they request during installation and to remove unused scopes.
evidence.quote: Your app must use all of the scopes that it requests during installation.

evidence.claim: Scope declaration: an OAuth app's required, conditionally required and optional scopes are reviewed on the Auth tab of the app in the Development section of the developer portal.
evidence.quote: Click the Auth tab, then review your app’s required, conditionally required, and optional scopes in the Scopes section.

evidence.claim: Private OAuth distribution can go up to 100 accounts if the app is created in a Solutions Partner portal; this override does not apply to static-auth private apps.
evidence.quote: up to 100 customer portals when the app is created in a Solutions Partner portal

evidence.claim: In the app config, at least one required scope must be declared and the installing user must grant required scopes; redirect URLs must use HTTPS, with http://localhost allowed for testing.
evidence.quote: Each app must have at least one auth redirect URL, and it must use HTTPS.

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs are declared in the app's auth config (redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json); the CLI sample uses http://localhost:3000/oauth-callback for local testing.
evidence.quote: Add one or more valid redirect URLs to the app-hsmeta.json file based on your local (or another non-production) OAuth server configuration.

evidence.claim: Apps can be created with the HubSpot CLI, where distribution (Marketplace vs. restricted to specific accounts) is selected during setup.
evidence.quote: select whether you plan to distribute your app on the HubSpot Marketplace or if want to restrict installation to specific HubSpot accounts.

evidence.claim: In the older developer portal flow, the app is created at the Applications page; name, description, redirect URL and scopes are set on the Auth tab, and client ID and secret are then issued.
evidence.quote: Once the app is created, you will see that some fields have been populated, you will need to get the Client ID, the Client secret

evidence.claim: Install URL includes client_id, redirect_uri and scope parameters at https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize; the code returned to the redirect URL is exchanged for access and refresh tokens.
evidence.quote: After a user authorizes your app and installs it into their account, the redirect URL will be appended with a code query parameter

evidence.claim: The install URL is found in the app's settings and is the link to send installers.
evidence.quote: a user can install it into their HubSpot account using the install URL located in your app’s settings

evidence.claim: Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth default scope set is broad and includes settings.users.write and many CRM write scopes, so a custom app should narrow scopes.
Marketplace listing removes the 25-install cap once approved; alternatives for growth are private OAuth distribution or Service Keys for tightly controlled internal use.
evidence.quote: Submit your app for a Marketplace listing, which removes the 25-install cap on marketplace distribution once your listing is approved.

evidence.claim: A private-distribution project app can later be switched to Marketplace distribution without interrupting existing installs (HubSpot community announcement).
evidence.quote: You can also start with a private distribution project-based app and switch it to marketplace distribution later

evidence.claim: Developer account prerequisite: a HubSpot developer account is needed to create and manage apps (per HubSpot's sample-app README).
evidence.quote: The first steps is to create a HubSpot developer account.

evidence.claim: Install permission: a standard-account install can be done by a Super Admin or a user with the HubSpot Marketplace access permission.
evidence.quote: The following users can install an app in a standard HubSpot account: Super admins

evidence.claim: Marketplace submissions are manually reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and are rejected if they do not meet the listed criteria.
evidence.quote: App listing submissions are manually reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and will be rejected if they do not meet the criteria outlined below.

evidence.claim: Only one app can be submitted at a time; additional apps submitted while the first is processing are automatically rejected.
evidence.quote: Any additional apps submitted while the initial app is being processed will automatically be rejected.

open_questions: Access token and refresh token lifetimes were not found, and PKCE support was not confirmed.
Exact developer account prerequisites (free vs. paid, Super Admin or developer seats) were not confirmed from an official page.

Conflicting guidance: the listing rules say no sensitive-data scopes, while the sensitive-data page says legacy and 2025.2 apps intended for Marketplace must request specific sensitive scopes from Ecosystem Quality. Whether 2025.2 apps can get them, and how long approval takes, is not documented.
Certification cost and the total Marketplace review timeline beyond the 10-business-day initial target were not confirmed. A third-party blog cites up to 60 days after feedback, unverified.
Common rejection reasons beyond the published criteria were not documented.
The certification page says 60 installs and six months; the listing minimum is three installs. A third-party claim about a May 2024 change could not be verified.
The HubSpot token endpoint (https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token) comes from Composio's config and was not checked on a HubSpot page.
The developer portal Applications page needs a logged-in portal and was not probed.
Verified-domain setup steps were not fetched in detail.
Composio's custom-auth UI steps (where to enter client ID and secret) were not researched.
